name: DR CONGO

flag.title: DRC Flag
flag.note: Sky blue, diagonal red stripe edged gold

lead: DR Congo is a giant rainforest nation in the heart of Africa. The Congo River snakes through jungles so vast they act like a second lung for our planet. More kinds of birds, fish, and primates live here than almost anywhere else, and beneath the floor lies a treasure chest of minerals that power the world's phones and batteries.

sections.geography: A river runs through it all

geo: The Congo River loops through the country like a giant question mark, draining a rainforest the size of Western Europe. Rains fall almost every day near the equator, keeping rivers brimming year-round.

To the east, the land rises into volcanoes and the Rwenzori 'Mountains of the Moon' — capped with glaciers right on the equator. Deep lakes like Tanganyika glitter between the peaks along the Great Rift Valley.
animals: The DRC is the only place where okapis roam wild — shy, zebra-striped relatives of the giraffe. Mountain gorillas cling on in the Virunga volcanoes, and the Congo River holds over 700 fish species, including the fearsome goliath tigerfish.

Bonobos — our closest ape relatives — live only in forests south of the Congo River. Forest elephants, hippos, and the Congo peacock (found nowhere else on Earth) complete an astonishing wildlife roster.
culture: Congo gave the world soukous — bouncy electric-guitar music that swept across Africa in the 1970s and still fills dance floors today. Kinshasa's sapeurs dress in spectacular tailored suits as living art and peaceful protest.
Over 200 ethnic groups produce carved wooden masks for ceremonies connecting the living with ancestors. Colourful wax-print kitenge fabrics are worn daily and inspire fashion designers worldwide.
history: The Kongo Kingdom ruled much of Central Africa for centuries, trading copper and cloth across the continent. In the 1880s Belgian King Leopold II seized the land, forcing people to harvest rubber in conditions so brutal that millions died.

Congo gained independence on 30 June 1960. Leader Patrice Lumumba gave a bold speech demanding true freedom. Decades of dictatorship followed, but elections have been held and vast mineral wealth offers hope.
wows: The Congo River plunges over 220 m deep — the deepest river on Earth.
DR Congo holds more than half of Africa's tropical rainforest.
No other river system on Earth has more freshwater fish species.
Kinshasa and Brazzaville are the world's closest pair of capital cities.
Almost every smartphone battery contains coltan mined in eastern Congo.
Bonobos are the only great apes known to be led by females.
Mount Nyiragongo holds one of Earth's largest active lava lakes, glowing orange at night.

myths.fact: The east has glaciated mountains, active volcanoes, and high grasslands — dramatically different from the rainforest basin.
Most of the country, including Kinshasa, is peaceful and welcoming; conflict is focused in specific eastern border zones.
